items.stem: A marketplace moderates listings in six languages. The rules change every month. The team must update the rules without new labeled training data. Which design meets the constraint?
options: Retrain a custom classifier for each language after every rule change.
Use the built-in safety classifiers as the marketplace rules.
Put the written rules and edge-case examples in the prompt, and constrain the verdict with a JSON schema.
Put the written rules in the prompt, and have a person approve every verdict before a listing goes live.
items.rationale: The written rules and examples in the prompt are the control, so a rule change needs an edit to text, not new training data. A JSON schema keeps each verdict parseable.
items.trap: A custom classifier for each language looks rigorous, but each rule change then needs new labels and a new training cycle.

items.stem: A compliance dashboard must count declined requests by policy area. The team cannot change the model. Which method meets the constraint?
options: HTTP error responses look like the standard count, since each declined request returns an error status code.
Read stop_reason on each response, and count the stop_details category when stop_reason is refusal.
Read the category value from the usage field, which lists the policy area of each call.
Log every full prompt, response, and header for each call, then sort the logs by policy area.
items.rationale: A decline arrives as a regular response with the stop reason refusal, not as an error. The stop_details category names the policy area, so the count needs no error parsing.
items.trap: HTTP error responses look like the standard count, but a decline returns a normal response with a stop reason.

items.stem: A release review asks for evidence that the product works for each user group. The review also asks which model the product uses. Select two actions that meet both requests.
options: Build an evaluation set with a group label for each user group, and set a floor for each group.
Cite the model system card as the fairness result for product users.
Request subgroup fairness metrics that Anthropic publishes for each Claude model.
Record the model system card link and the exact model ID in the release record.
items.rationale: The per-group evaluation tests the product on its own users, and a floor blocks a release that fails one group. (Inference) The system card and the exact model ID document the model that the product uses.
items.trap: A system card cited as fairness evidence looks sufficient, but the card describes model tests, not the product users.
